# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("ElKhateeb_2023_tacrolimus"))$reference`
* Description (base model): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("ElKhateeb_2023_tacrolimus"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1097/FTD.0000000000001108> (open access, PMC10635338)

El-Khateeb et al. combined a bottom-up (PBPK-style) description of tacrolimus
disposition with a top-down population fit of routine therapeutic-drug-monitoring
troughs. Everything except the hepatic unbound intrinsic clearance `CLint` is
computed from patient data at every trough: hepatic blood flow from body weight,
the blood:plasma ratio from hematocrit, the unbound fraction from albumin, renal
clearance from eGFR, and the steady-state volume from a Rodgers tissue
composition. `CLint` was then estimated in Monolix with between-subject and
inter-occasion variability, and three covariate models for kidney function on
`CLint` were compared in parallel against the base model (Supplementary File 3,
Figure 2).

The library carries three of the four fits, one file each:

| Model | Covariate on CLint | Table 1 row | AIC |
|-------|--------------------|-------------|-----|
| `ElKhateeb_2023_tacrolimus` | none (base model) | Base | 7297.1 |
| `ElKhateeb_2023_tacrolimus_egfr` | eGFR, continuous | eGFR | 7249.14 |
| `ElKhateeb_2023_tacrolimus_ckdstage` | CKD stage 1-5, categorical | CKD stage | 7264.74 |

The fourth, CKD group (stable vs failing transplant), was non-significant
(beta = -0.0073, RSE 1880%) and is the base model in all but name, so it is
not packaged.

# Population

Forty adult renal transplant recipients from the Salford Royal Hospital
transplant database (UK), 20 with stable graft function and 20 with failing
graft function (annual eGFR fall above 5 mL/min/1.73 m^2), matched for age,
sex and ethnicity. Median age 41.6 years (IQR 33.6-50.9), 57.5% male, 77.5%
white; baseline eGFR median 45 mL/min/1.73 m^2 (IQR 34.5-55.5), hematocrit 0.36
(0.32-0.41) and albumin 43 g/L (40-45) (Results; Supplementary File 3 Table 2).
All received immediate-release tacrolimus (Prograf) twice daily, 2-14 mg/day.
The analysis used 1167 steady-state whole-blood troughs (median 29 per patient)
over a median 3.3-year follow-up, during which eGFR ranged 4.97-119.2
mL/min/1.73 m^2 (CKD stages 1-5). Troughs were normalised to 5 mg every 12 h.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("ElKhateeb_2023_tacrolimus")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source. The
bottom-up formulas and constants come from the authors' calculation
spreadsheet (Supplementary File 1) and agree with the printed equations; the
structural closed form is the Monolix script (Supplementary File 2).

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Trough at steady state | `Dose * F * exp(-kel*tau) / (Vss,b * (1 - exp(-kel*tau)))` | Eq. 3 and 17; Supplementary File 2 |
| `f(central)` = F | `fa * (1 - egut) * (1 - CLh,b/Qh)` | Eq. 4-5 |
| `fa` | 1 (fixed) | Methods below Eq. 5 |
| `egut` | 0.86 (fixed; fg = 0.14) | Methods below Eq. 5 |
| `kel` | `(CLr,b + CLh,b) / Vss,b` | Eq. 6 |
| `CLr,b` | `fub * eGFR` (L/h/1.73 m^2) | Eq. 7 |
| `CLh,b` | `Qh * fub * CLint / (Qh + fub * CLint)` | Eq. 8 (well-stirred liver) |
| `fub` | `fup / (B/P)` | Eq. 9 |
| `fup` | `1 / (1 + (ALB/45) * (1 - 0.013)/0.013)` | Eq. 10 |
| `Vss,b` | `(Vp + Ve * E:P + 10 * sum(Vt * Pt:p)) / (B/P)` | Eq. 11; scaling factor 10 in Methods |
| `Vp`, `Ve` | `Vb * (1 - Hct)`, `Vb * Hct` | Eq. 12-13 |
| `Vb` | sex-specific in height (m) and weight | Eq. 14-15 |
| `B/P` | `E:P * Hct + (1 - Hct)`, E:P = 77.27 | Eq. 16; Supplementary File 1 |
| Organ masses, densities | ICRP female 60 kg / male 73 kg, scaled by WT | Supplementary File 1 |
| `Pt:p` (13 tissues) | 0.52-1.91 | Supplementary File 3 Table 1 |
| `Qh` | `0.227 * 187 * WT^0.81` mL/min | Supplementary File 2 |
| `lclint` | log(5886.7) / log(4350.89) / log(6377.46) | Table 1 Base / eGFR / CKD stage |
| `e_crcl_clint` | 0.11 per L/h/1.73 m^2 | Table 1 eGFR row (form: see Assumptions) |
| `e_ckd2_clint` ... `e_ckd5_clint` | -0.047, -0.011, -0.1, -0.19, -0.31 | Table 1 CKD stage rows (sign: see Assumptions) |
| `etalclint` | 0.32^2 / 0.33^2 / 0.33^2 | Table 1 omega (Monolix SD) |
| `etaiov_lclint` | 0.2^2 / 0.18^2 / 0.19^2 | Table 1 gamma (Monolix SD) |
| `propSd` | 0.101 / 0.109 / 0.105 | Not reported; see Assumptions |

# Bottom-up quantities

The model computes the authors' per-trough regressors internally from six
covariates (`WT`, `HT`, `SEXF`, `HCT`, `ALB`, `CRCL`). The virtual cohort below
draws them from the distributions of the 1167 measurements in Supplementary
File 1 (weight median 73 kg, log-SD 0.23; height median 173 cm in men and 160
cm in women; hematocrit mean 0.364, SD 0.055; albumin mean 42.3 g/L, SD 4.9;
eGFR median 38.6 mL/min/1.73 m^2, log-SD 0.51; about half the measurements
from men).

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20231108)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20231108)
n_sub <- 200
cohort <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  SEXF = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 0.5),
  HT = ifelse(SEXF == 1, rnorm(n_sub, 160, 6), rnorm(n_sub, 173, 6)),
  WT = pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n_sub, log(73), 0.23)), 40), 141),
  HCT = 100 * pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_sub, 0.364, 0.055), 0.21), 0.59),
  ALB = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_sub, 42.3, 4.9), 19), 53),
  CRCL = pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n_sub, log(38.6), 0.51)), 5), 119)
)

# The same formulas as model(), written out once so the vignette can check
# the model's internal quantities against the paper's summary numbers.
bottom_up <- function(d, kp_scale = 10, clint = 5886.7) {
  hct <- d$HCT / 100
  bpr <- 77.27 * hct + 1 - hct
  fup <- 1 / (1 + (d$ALB / 45) * (1 - 0.013) / 0.013)
  fub <- fup / bpr
  vb <- ifelse(d$SEXF == 1,
    0.3561 * (d$HT / 100)^3 + 0.03308 * d$WT + 0.1833,
    0.3669 * (d$HT / 100)^3 + 0.03219 * d$WT + 0.6041
  )
  mass_f <- c(22500, 7800, 1300, 1965, 250, 275, 1400, 420, 120, 17500, 2300, 130, 4040) / 60
  mass_m <- c(18200, 10500, 1450, 2110, 330, 310, 1800, 500, 140, 29000, 3300, 150, 5210) / 73
  dens <- c(950, 1920, 1050, 1040, 1050, 1050, 1070, 384, 1050, 1050, 1090, 1040, 1050)
  kp <- c(1.90, 1.89, 1.91, 1.56, 0.74, 0.96, 1.33, 0.52, 1.37, 0.96, 1.07, 0.97, 1.90)
  vtkp <- ifelse(d$SEXF == 1, sum(mass_f / dens * kp), sum(mass_m / dens * kp))
  vss_b <- (vb * (1 - hct) + vb * hct * 77.27 + kp_scale * d$WT * vtkp) / bpr
  qh <- 0.227 * 187 * d$WT^0.81 * 0.06
  clh <- qh * fub * clint / (qh + fub * clint)
  clr <- fub * d$CRCL * 0.06
  fbio <- 0.14 * (1 - clh / qh)
  kel <- (clh + clr) / vss_b
  tibble(bpr, fup, fub, vss_b, qh, clh, fbio, kel,
    trough = 5000 * fbio * exp(-kel * 12) / (vss_b * (1 - exp(-kel * 12)))
  )
}
bu <- bottom_up(cohort)
bu_unscaled <- bottom_up(cohort, kp_scale = 1)

checks <- tibble(
  Quantity = c(
    "Mean B/P", "Mean Vss,b before the x10 Pt:p scaling (L)",
    "Mean CLh,b at CLintpop of the base model (L/h)"
  ),
  Paper = c(28.8, 8.2, 2.84),
  Source = c("Results, B/P 19-46", "Methods, after Eq. 16", "Discussion (2.84 +/- 0.94)"),
  Simulated = c(mean(bu$bpr), mean(bu_unscaled$vss_b), mean(bu$clh))
)
knitr::kable(checks, digits = 2, caption = "Bottom-up quantities in the virtual cohort vs the paper.")
stopifnot(
  # Each is a cohort mean of a smooth function of covariates whose spread the
  # cohort reproduces, so a wrong constant (E:P, a Pt:p, a density, the 0.227
  # hepatic fraction of cardiac output) moves it by far more than 10%.
  abs(mean(bu$bpr) / 28.8 - 1) < 0.10,
  abs(mean(bu_unscaled$vss_b) / 8.2 - 1) < 0.10,
  abs(mean(bu$clh) / 2.84 - 1) < 0.10
)
```

# The ODE reproduces the closed form

The packaged model is a one-compartment ODE with the dose entering the central
compartment (absorption complete within the interval) and `f(central)` equal to
the bottom-up bioavailability. At steady state on 5 mg every 12 h its
end-of-interval concentration must equal Eq. 17 for every subject.

```{r closed-form}
mod_base <- readModelDb("ElKhateeb_2023_tacrolimus")

ev_cf <- cohort |>
  mutate(OCC = 1) |>
  tidyr::crossing(evid = c(1, 0)) |>
  mutate(
    time = ifelse(evid == 1, 0, 12), amt = ifelse(evid == 1, 5, 0),
    ss = ifelse(evid == 1, 1, 0), ii = ifelse(evid == 1, 12, 0), cmt = "central"
  ) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
# Two occasion levels are needed for the nested IOV; the typical-value solve
# ignores them.
ev_cf$OCC[ev_cf$id %% 2 == 0] <- 2

sim_cf <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_base), ev_cf,
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, ssRtol = 1e-10, ssAtol = 1e-12, maxsteps = 1e6,
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
rel_err <- sim_cf$Cc / bu$trough - 1
max(abs(rel_err))
stopifnot(max(abs(rel_err)) < 1e-6)
```

# Covariate effects on CLint

Figure 4 of the paper relates the individual CLint estimates to eGFR and CKD
stage. The packaged covariate models give the typical CLint below; the paper's
per-stage means are averages of individual (empirical Bayes) estimates, so they
carry the random effects and are compared only for direction and size.

```{r covariate-effects}
mod_egfr <- readModelDb("ElKhateeb_2023_tacrolimus_egfr")
mod_ckd <- readModelDb("ElKhateeb_2023_tacrolimus_ckdstage")
th_egfr <- rxode2::rxode(mod_egfr)$theta
th_ckd <- rxode2::rxode(mod_ckd)$theta

clint_egfr <- function(egfr) exp(th_egfr[["lclint"]] + th_egfr[["e_crcl_clint"]] * egfr * 0.06)
stage_coef <- c(
  "1" = 0, "2" = th_ckd[["e_ckd2_clint"]], "3a" = th_ckd[["e_ckd3a_clint"]],
  "3b" = th_ckd[["e_ckd3b_clint"]], "4" = th_ckd[["e_ckd4_clint"]], "5" = th_ckd[["e_ckd5_clint"]]
)
stage_tab <- tibble(
  `CKD stage` = names(stage_coef),
  `Typical CLint, CKD-stage model (L/h)` = exp(th_ckd[["lclint"]] + stage_coef),
  `Mean individual CLint, paper (L/h)` = c(7483, 6639, 6410, 5944, 6039, 4754)
)
knitr::kable(stage_tab, digits = 0, caption = "CLint by CKD stage (paper values: Results, Figure 4A).")

ggplot(tibble(egfr = seq(5, 120, by = 1)), aes(egfr, clint_egfr(egfr))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(
    data = tibble(egfr = c(100, 75, 52.5, 37.5, 22.5, 10), clint = stage_tab$`Typical CLint, CKD-stage model (L/h)`),
    aes(egfr, clint), colour = "firebrick"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m^2)", y = "Typical CLint (L/h)",
    caption = "Line: eGFR model. Points: CKD-stage model at mid-stage eGFR. Compare Figure 4A/4C of El-Khateeb 2023."
  )

# Results: 'A 50% decrease in eGFR was associated with a 15% decrease in
# CLint'. Evaluated from the baseline median eGFR of 45 mL/min/1.73 m^2.
drop_half <- 1 - clint_egfr(45 / 2) / clint_egfr(45)
drop_half
# Results: 'CLint decreased by 36% in stage 5 CKD patients from stage 1'
# (individual means); the typical-value ratio of the stage model.
drop_stage5 <- 1 - exp(stage_coef[["5"]])
drop_stage5
stopifnot(
  # The uncentred exponential gives 12-15% over the cohort's eGFR range; the
  # printed centred power form would give 7%.
  drop_half > 0.10, drop_half < 0.20,
  # Restored negative signs: stage 5 lower than stage 1.
  drop_stage5 > 0.2, drop_stage5 < 0.4,
  abs(stage_tab$`Typical CLint, CKD-stage model (L/h)`[6] / 4754 - 1) < 0.05
)
```

# Dose-normalised trough VPC

Supplementary File 3 Figure 3 is the prediction-corrected VPC of the base model:
dose-adjusted troughs scatter around a median of about 13 ng/mL with a 95%
band of roughly 6-30 ng/mL, flat over the follow-up. The 1167 observed troughs
in Supplementary File 1 have median 12.9 ng/mL, 2.5th percentile 3.9 and 97.5th
percentile 39.8 ng/mL. Each virtual subject below contributes six troughs, one
per occasion, each after steady-state dosing at 5 mg every 12 h.

```{r vpc}
n_occ <- 6
ev_vpc <- cohort |>
  tidyr::crossing(OCC = seq_len(n_occ), evid = c(1, 0)) |>
  mutate(
    time = (OCC - 1) * 5000 + ifelse(evid == 1, 0, 12),
    amt = ifelse(evid == 1, 5, 0), ss = ifelse(evid == 1, 1, 0),
    ii = ifelse(evid == 1, 12, 0), cmt = "central"
  ) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_vpc <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_base, ev_vpc, maxsteps = 1e6, returnType = "data.frame")

troughs <- sim_vpc |> filter(!is.na(sim))
vpc_tab <- tibble(
  Statistic = c("2.5th percentile", "Median", "97.5th percentile"),
  `Observed, Supplementary File 1 (ng/mL)` = c(3.9, 12.86, 39.77),
  `Simulated, base model (ng/mL)` = quantile(troughs$sim, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
)
knitr::kable(vpc_tab, digits = 1, caption = "Dose-normalised troughs: simulated vs observed.")

ggplot(troughs, aes(time / 24, sim)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15, colour = "darkgreen") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = quantile(troughs$sim, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)), linetype = c(2, 1, 2)) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)", y = "Dose-adjusted trough (ng/mL)",
    caption = "Replicates the layout of Supplementary File 3 Figure 3 of El-Khateeb 2023 (base model)."
  )

stopifnot(
  # Centre: a wrong CLint, volume or bioavailability term moves the median
  # by tens of percent.
  abs(median(troughs$sim) / 12.86 - 1) < 0.20,
  # Envelope, on robust quantiles of 1200 simulated troughs.
  quantile(troughs$sim, 0.975) > 25, quantile(troughs$sim, 0.975) < 60,
  quantile(troughs$sim, 0.025) > 2, quantile(troughs$sim, 0.025) < 7
)
```

# PKNCA: steady-state interval by CKD stage

The paper reports no NCA. The steady-state dosing interval of a typical patient
in each CKD stage (CKD-stage model, median covariates, eGFR at mid-stage) is
summarised with PKNCA; `cmin` must equal the closed-form trough and `auclast`
must equal `F * Dose / CL` for the interval.

```{r pknca}
typ <- tibble(
  treatment = c("1", "2", "3a", "3b", "4", "5"),
  CRCL = c(100, 75, 52.5, 37.5, 22.5, 10),
  id = seq_along(CRCL), SEXF = 0, HT = 173, WT = 73, HCT = 36, ALB = 43
)
grid <- seq(0, 12, by = 0.25)
ev_nca <- bind_rows(
  typ |> mutate(time = 0, evid = 1, amt = 5, ss = 1, ii = 12),
  typ |> tidyr::crossing(time = grid) |> mutate(evid = 0, amt = 0, ss = 0, ii = 0)
) |>
  mutate(cmt = "central", OCC = ifelse(id %% 2 == 0, 2, 1)) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_nca <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_ckd), ev_nca,
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, ssRtol = 1e-10, ssAtol = 1e-12, maxsteps = 1e6,
  keep = "treatment", returnType = "data.frame"
)

conc_df <- sim_nca |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_df <- ev_nca |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 12, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

# Closed-form references at the typical CLint of each stage.
ref <- typ |>
  mutate(clint = exp(th_ckd[["lclint"]] + stage_coef[treatment]))
ref_bu <- bind_cols(ref, bottom_up(ref, clint = ref$clint) |> select(-qh))
ref_bu <- ref_bu |>
  mutate(
    cmin_ref = trough,
    auc_ref = 1000 * 5 * fbio / (kel * vss_b)
  )
nca_cmp <- nca_wide |>
  left_join(ref_bu |> select(treatment, cmin_ref, auc_ref), by = "treatment")

nca_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "CKD stage" = treatment,
    "Cmax (ng/mL)" = cmax,
    "Cmin (ng/mL)" = cmin,
    "AUC0-12 (ng*h/mL)" = auclast,
    "Closed-form trough (ng/mL)" = cmin_ref,
    "F * Dose / CL (ng*h/mL)" = auc_ref
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Steady-state interval, typical patient by CKD stage (5 mg every 12 h).")

stopifnot(
  # cmin is the solved end-of-interval value: numerical error only.
  max(abs(nca_cmp$cmin / nca_cmp$cmin_ref - 1)) < 1e-6,
  # linear-up/log-down trapezoid on a 0.25 h grid of a mono-exponential.
  max(abs(nca_cmp$auclast / nca_cmp$auc_ref - 1)) < 0.01
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Residual-error magnitude is not published.** The paper names the selected
  residual model ("proportional") but reports no value for it in Table 1,
  Supplementary File 3 Table 3 or anywhere else. The maintainers estimated it
  by profile likelihood on the authors' own per-measurement dataset
  (Supplementary File 1), holding CLintpop, omega and gamma at each model's
  Table 1 values and integrating the between-subject and per-trough
  inter-occasion effects by quadrature. Giving that dataset to the model
  reproduces the published fit closely: with the profiled value the marginal
  -2LL of the base model is 7266 against the published 7289.1, and freeing
  omega and gamma as well returns 0.31 and 0.21 against the published 0.32 and
  0.20. The resulting `propSd` (0.101 base, 0.109 eGFR, 0.105 CKD stage) is
  extractor-derived, not a published estimate.
- **Error model form.** The paper states that "observations were assumed to
  follow a log-normal distribution", which in Monolix makes the "proportional"
  error model proportional on the log-transformed prediction. The model encodes
  that as `Cc ~ lnorm(NA) + propT(propSd)`. On the authors' dataset this form
  fits about 45 -2LL units better than a proportional error on the untransformed
  scale, and its freely estimated omega and gamma (0.31, 0.21) sit closer to
  the published values than those of the untransformed form (0.31, 0.25).
- **eGFR covariate form.** Eq. 19 prints a power model centred at the median
  eGFR, `(eGFR/median)^beta`. With beta = 0.11 that form changes CLint by less
  than 10% across the cohort, which leaves CLintpop = 4350.89 L/h 26% below
  the base model everywhere and contradicts both the reported likelihood gain
  and the Results statement that halving eGFR lowers CLint by 15%. Monolix's
  default for a continuous covariate on a log-normal parameter, the uncentred
  `exp(beta * eGFR)` with eGFR in L/h/1.73 m^2 (the unit of the script's
  regressor), reproduces all three: typical CLint 5600 L/h at the median eGFR,
  a 12-15% fall per halving, and a -2LL drop of 55 from the base model on the
  authors' dataset against the published 50 (the centred power form drops it
  by 2). The model uses the uncentred exponential.
- **CKD-stage coefficient signs.** Table 1 prints the stage coefficients
  without signs. Read as positive in Eq. 20 they would raise CLint with
  advancing CKD, the opposite of the paper's conclusion. The model uses them
  as negative; the stage-5 typical CLint, 4677 L/h, then matches the reported
  stage-5 mean of 4754 L/h, and on the authors' dataset the negative set lowers
  -2LL by 45 from the base model (published 42) while the positive set raises
  it by 160.
- **CKD stage is derived from eGFR** inside the model with the thresholds of
  the authors' spreadsheet (90, 60, 45, 30, 15 mL/min/1.73 m^2), which is how
  the stage column of Supplementary File 1 was computed per measurement.
- **E:P = 77.27**, the value the authors' spreadsheet uses to compute every
  blood:plasma ratio in the fitted dataset; the text quotes the fit as 77.4.
- **eGFR enters renal clearance unadjusted for body surface area**
  (L/h/1.73 m^2 used as L/h), as in the Monolix script. Renal clearance is
  below 0.1% of total tacrolimus clearance, so this has no practical effect.
- **Absorption.** The paper simplifies its first-order-absorption trough
  equation by assuming absorption is complete within the dosing interval and
  never estimates ka, so the dose enters `central` directly with
  `f(central)` equal to the bottom-up bioavailability. Concentrations within
  the interval (in particular Cmax) are therefore those of an instantaneous
  input and should not be read as predictions of the real oral peak; the model
  is built for troughs.
- **Inter-occasion variability** uses the native nested random effect
  `etaiov_lclint ~ ... | OCC`, with one occasion per trough as in the paper.
  Event tables must carry an `OCC` column with at least two distinct values.
  The library's convention checker reports `OCC` as a covariate not referenced
  in `model()`, because it is consumed by the `ini()` nesting syntax.
- **Virtual cohort.** Height and weight are not tabulated in the article; the
  cohort's covariate distributions are summaries of the per-measurement
  spreadsheet (Supplementary File 1), and covariates are held constant within
  each virtual subject. The covariates are drawn independently of one another,
  so the cohort lacks the correlations of the real patients, which is one
  reason the simulated 97.5th percentile of the dose-normalised trough (about
  45-50 ng/mL) runs above the observed 39.8 ng/mL while the median matches.
- No erratum or correction notice for this article was found in Europe PMC
  (no linked correction on PMID 37315152; checked 2026-10-28).
